content.page_summary: Discussion of randomized trials and meta-analyses assessing complete revascularization strategies in patients with multivessel ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) undergoing primary PCI (PPCI), comparing FFR-guided versus angiography-guided approaches and implications for timing of non-IRA PCI.

FLOWER-MI.design: Randomized trial of patients undergoing PPCI with multivessel disease (MVD) assigned to complete revascularization guided by FFR versus angiography.
FLOWER-MI.key_findings: An FFR-guided strategy did not reduce the risk of death, MI, or urgent revascularization at 1 year compared with an angiography-guided approach.

procedural_data.complete_revascularization_index_procedu: Only performed in 4% of patients in both groups
procedural_data.functional_evaluation_timing: Mainly undertaken at time of second procedure

FLOWER-MI.timing_note: Study design allowed staged complete revascularization as early as possible before discharge and within 5 days of initial procedure.

meta_analyses.description: Meta-analysis of 10 RCTs (including patients undergoing PPCI) comparing complete revascularization vs IRA-only PCI.
meta_analyses.finding: Preventive PCI of the non-IRA was associated with a significant reduction in cardiac death and non-fatal MI only when the decision to proceed with non-IRA PCI was based solely on angiography (not angiography plus FFR).

meta_analyses.description: Another meta-analysis of seven RCTs assessing patients undergoing PPCI
meta_analyses.finding: Reported similar findings regarding benefit of angiography-based decisions for non-IRA PCI.

meta_analyses.description: Meta-analysis (pre-dating FLOWER-MI) examining heterogeneity of primary outcome by strategy
meta_analyses.finding: No heterogeneity in primary outcome when complete revascularization was performed using an FFR-guided strategy (OR 0.78, 95% CI 0.43–1.44) or an angiography-guided strategy (OR 0.61, 95% CI 0.38–0.97); P = 0.52 for interaction.

post_hoc_patient_level_analysis.strategy: Functionally complete revascularization (PCI of stenosis with FFR ≤0.80; deferral to medical therapy if FFR >0.80)
post_hoc_patient_level_analysis.finding: Residual SYNTAX score (proxy of residual coronary stenosis deferred to medical therapy) was not associated with MACE at 2 years, suggesting it may be safe to defer management of functionally non-significant stenoses in the non-IRA.

FRAME_AMI.name: FRAME AMI (FFR Versus Angiography-Guided Strategy for Management of AMI With Multivessel Disease)
FRAME_AMI.comparison: Selective PCI guided by FFR (PCI if FFR ≤0.80) versus routine PCI guided by angiography (PCI if diameter stenosis >50%) for non-IRA lesions in patients presenting with AMI who had successful PCI of the IRA.
FRAME_AMI.population_details: Patients presenting with AMI who had undergone successful PCI of the IRA (47% STEMI, 53% NSTEMI).
FRAME_AMI.key_result: Primary endpoint occurred less frequently in patients randomized to the FFR-guided strategy, mainly driven by differences in patients presenting with NSTEMI.
FRAME_AMI.limitations: Trial was terminated early with only 562 of intended 1292 patients enrolled; relatively small number of primary outcome events.

clinical_implications: Complete revascularization during PPCI can be performed either at index procedure or staged; study designs often allowed staged procedures within days.
Evidence suggests benefit of preventive non-IRA PCI depends on how lesions are selected (angiography alone vs physiology-guided with FFR).

FFR-guided strategies do not uniformly show superiority over angiography-guided strategies for reduction in death/MI/urgent revascularization at 1 year (FLOWER-MI) but other analyses and trials show mixed results depending on population and endpoints.
Deferring PCI for lesions that are not functionally significant (FFR >0.80) appears safe in pooled post-hoc analyses with respect to 2-year MACE.
FRAME AMI suggests possible long-term benefit of FFR-guided selective PCI but was underpowered due to early termination; findings driven largely by NSTEMI subgroup.
